title: Language's editor edits one record of a source file in place, and `draftSource` refuses values that would add structure
summary: @inventarch/language/editor exports appendRecord(text, draft), addRelationship(text, identity, spelling, target), setField(text, identity, path, value, schema, append?), annotateRecord(text, identity, comment), encodeValue(field, text, item?), draftValue(field, text), relationshipConsent(registry, word, spelling, target, fragment?) and SourceEditError, with the DraftSchema, DraftField, SourceEditReason and RelationshipConsent types; @inventarch/runtime/editor re-exports those functions, SourceEditError and the four types, with draftSource and VERB_PHRASES, for hosts that may not import the language package. The language root also exports isNumberText, isQualifiedName and isIsoDate, the number, qname and iso-date rules compliance applies, and @inventarch/compliance's value checks now use them (its verdicts are unchanged). Each edit takes one whole .ia file that parses and returns it again with exactly one top-level record, named `@word name`, changed: a draftSource draft appended after one blank line (an empty file gets the draft's pragma, and a last line with no line ending gains one), one row added to the record's relationships section (or a new section at the record's end), one schema field set as <section>.<key> (append adds one item to a list field, creating it when absent), or one comment line put above the record, replacing one there with the same first word. The edit is spliced into the file as it is: every other line keeps its bytes and line ending, a byte-order mark stays, and only the edited record is formatted, in the file's line ending, so only its digest can move; a trailing comment on a one-line field being replaced is kept. encodeValue is the strict, opt-in spelling setField uses: text is always quoted, and every other type must parse as exactly one value of it by the predicates compliance applies (an id and its `in` set, a reference and its `to` word, a qname, a number, a flag, a list of one, the iso-date form), an id, qname or number written quoted being spelled bare, with nothing after it; line breaks, C0 and C1 controls but the tab, DEL, the Unicode line and paragraph separators and the bidirectional embedding, override and isolate controls are refused. A refused edit throws SourceEditError with a closed reason (parse, identity, nested, field, value, repeated, duplicate, spelling, target, structure) and returns no text: an undeclared field, a value of another type, a field, section or record the file states twice, a relationship row the section already holds word for word, a duplicate list item or record, a conditional or structured field, a comment inside a multi-line value being replaced, a nested record, an unknown verb, and a target that is neither a canonical identity nor `@word name` (either with an optional fragment). relationshipConsent judges one row by the two-sided consent rule admission applies and names the refusing side and the system that registers its word. Bug fix: draftSource (and so @inventarch/runtime/editor's EditorWorkspace.draft) spells each value through draftValue, which writes it as 2.0.0 did (text quoted, every other type as given) but refuses, with SourceEditError, a value that would add structure: a `when` condition or a comment, which 2.0.0 wrote into the draft, as it already refused a line break; EditorWorkspace.draft reports that refusal as EditorError 'invalid'. Limits: only top-level records are edited; a relationship row that differs from one already there only in spelling (a canonical identity for a reference, a different case) is left to admission; consent and admission are the caller's to compile and report (no IA-LANG diagnostic code is added); the file must parse, and only the edited record is reformatted.
